title: Pharma Distribution Analytics · dbt + DuckDB
summary: Raw ERP extracts for a fictional Istanbul pharmaceutical wholesaler turned into a tested dbt star schema with an SCD Type 2 pharmacy dimension, OTIF delivery and expiry-loss marts. 54 nodes, 39 data tests, CI on every push.
question: Is the wholesaler delivering on time and in full, which warehouse is behind, and which products lose the most value to expired returns, while pharmacy master data keeps changing underneath?
approach: Land six ERP extracts and read them directly with DuckDB external sources.
Clean in staging: 19 district spellings to 8, mixed-case codes, 44 duplicated order lines.
Track pharmacy changes with a dbt snapshot (SCD Type 2) and a surrogate key per version.
Model order-line and delivery facts at their own grain, then OTIF and expiry-risk marts.
Guard everything with generic, custom generic and singular tests that run in CI.
result: On-time delivery 86.7 % and OTIF 77.3 %. The European-side warehouse is the problem (83.3 % on time against 89.9 %). The top 10 SKUs account for 44.9 % of the ₺290 K lost to expired stock.
scope: All pharmacies, products and transactions are synthetic, generated to behave like a real ERP export.

title: Construction Cost Control · Earned Value
summary: Earned value management for six construction projects in Istanbul: a DuckDB model computing CPI, SPI, EAC and TCPI per work package, and a live dashboard with S-curves, a cost and schedule quadrant and change orders.
question: A cost report says how much was spent. It does not say whether that spending bought the progress it should have. Which projects are over budget, which are late, and where will they land?
approach: Model budget by WBS category, a planned S-curve, monthly progress, 740 invoices and change orders.
Compute PV, EV and AC per work package per month before rolling up, so a late package cannot hide behind an early one.
Derive CPI, SPI, EAC, VAC, TCPI and a health rule per project.
Publish an interactive dashboard on GitHub Pages and test the warehouse after every build.
result: Portfolio CPI 0.98 and SPI 0.89, forecast ₺92 M over budget. The tower is a cost problem (steel package CPI 0.83); the hospital is a schedule problem (SPI 0.67, finishing 15 months late at this pace).
scope: Six fictional projects with synthetic cost data. The problems modelled are typical of Istanbul building projects.

title: TCMB FX Rates Pipeline
summary: An incremental, idempotent pipeline that loads the Central Bank of Türkiye's daily exchange-rate bulletin into DuckDB every business day on GitHub Actions, checks the data and publishes a live dashboard.
question: Downloading one XML file is easy. Running it every day without supervision, through weekends, public holidays, outages and corrected bulletins, is the real work.
approach: Fetch each missing business day from the CBRT archive, starting from a watermark.
Record holidays (404) as settled so they are never re-requested; retry failed days.
Upsert on date and currency so reruns and corrected bulletins never duplicate rows.
Run quality checks, export CSV and JSON, and commit them from a scheduled GitHub Action.
result: First run backfilled 2026: 205 bulletins and 4,510 rates loaded, 13 public holidays recognised from the 404s (including the Ramadan and Sacrifice feasts), 0 failed days, all quality checks passed. It now refreshes itself every weekday after the 15:30 bulletin.
scope: Uses the CBRT's public indicative rates. Not affiliated with the CBRT and not investment advice.

title: Invoice Intake Automation
summary: Supplier invoices arrive as PDFs in three layouts. The pipeline reads them, checks 14 business rules against vendor and PO master data, books clean invoices into SQLite and routes the rest to an exceptions queue with the reason written out.
question: The expensive mistakes in accounts payable are not typos: paying the same invoice twice, paying against a used-up PO, or paying a total that does not add up.
approach: Extract text from each PDF and parse fields with Turkish and English label synonyms.
Normalise Turkish money and dates (1.234,56 and 31.12.2026).
Validate arithmetic, VAT, vendor tax ID, duplicates, PO existence, ownership and remaining budget.
Book or reject, record every file by SHA-256 so reruns are safe, and write an HTML run report.
result: On 40 sample invoices: 29 booked, 11 stopped with written reasons. Two over-billed POs were not seeded; they came from ordinary invoices adding up past the approved amount.
scope: Vendors, tax IDs and invoices are synthetic PDFs generated for the project.

title: CSV Data Profiler
summary: A pip-installable command that profiles any CSV or Excel file: inferred types, a quality score, ranked issues and a self-contained HTML report, with an exit code that turns it into a CI quality gate.
question: Before building a pipeline or a dashboard, the first question is always: can this file be trusted?
approach: Read every column as text first so type problems stay visible.
Infer types with a 90 % parse threshold.
Check duplicates, keys, missing values, label spellings, whitespace, dates, numbers stored as text and outliers.
Render a self-contained HTML report and expose --fail-on for CI.
result: On a deliberately messy 507-row order export it finds duplicate rows and keys, five cities written several ways, two date formats and prices stored with currency symbols.
scope: The example file is generated by a script in the repository.

title: Coffee Shop Chain Data Warehouse
summary: A data warehouse built from scratch for a coffee chain on PostgreSQL: raw, messy data through Bronze, Silver and Gold layers to an interactive Power BI dashboard for decision-making.
question: A chain with several branches records sales, products and staff in separate files. Before anyone can compare branches, the data has to agree on what a sale, a product and a day actually are.
approach: Land the raw files untouched in a Bronze schema so every later change can be traced back.
Clean types, trim text, remove duplicates and standardise categories in Silver.
Model a Gold star schema with conformed dimensions and a sales fact at line-item grain.
Build the Power BI report on Gold only, so every visual reads from tested tables.
result: A layered warehouse you can rebuild from scratch, with each transformation step in its own SQL script and a dashboard that reads from the curated layer.
scope: The dataset is a practice scenario designed for this project. Figures describe the scenario, not a real company.

title: Sales & Profit Executive Dashboard
summary: A single-file interactive dashboard from 500 order-level transactions over two years: 7 KPIs that recalculate with every filter, 7 charts, 8 filters and a key-insights panel computed live.
question: Executives need one page that answers where revenue comes from and where profit leaks, without opening a BI tool.
approach: Profile the 500-order dataset and fix the fields that drive revenue and profit.
Define each KPI once, so revenue, profit and margin are computed the same way everywhere.
Build a single HTML file with Chart.js so the report opens anywhere with no install.
Add filters so a reader can move from the total down to a category in two clicks.
result: 7 KPIs, 7 charts and 8 filters in one portable HTML file, with an insights panel that rewrites itself as filters change. Shared publicly on LinkedIn.
scope: Built on a 500-order retail practice dataset.

title: Logistics Performance Analytics
summary: A layered SQL Server pipeline (raw, clean, mart) on deliberately messy data for a fictional Turkish delivery company, with a 3-page Power BI dashboard that traced most delays to four drivers rather than specific cities.
question: Deliveries are late. Is it the cities, the routes or the people? The raw data can’t answer yet: city names are spelled five ways, dates come in mixed formats and some shipments point to drivers who don’t exist.
approach: Load the messy source as-is into a raw layer.
Standardise inconsistent city names and date formats, and remove duplicates in the clean layer.
Add “Unknown” members for orphan keys so no shipment silently disappears from totals.
Model a mart with a star schema and a date dimension, then build a 3-page Power BI dashboard with DAX measures.
result: 66% of shipments arrived on time, and four drivers, not specific cities, caused most of the delays. That moves the conversation from route planning to driver support.
scope: All records are synthetic, created for a fictional Turkish delivery company. The messiness is deliberate.

title: Global Health Indicators Report
summary: A Power BI report on a Global Health Indicators dataset, with Python cleaning that removes World Bank aggregate rows and handles nulls before modelling.
question: Public datasets mix countries with regional aggregates. Counting both twice quietly distorts every average.
approach: Remove World Bank aggregate rows in Python so only real countries remain.
Decide how to treat each kind of null instead of dropping rows blindly.
Write DAX measures for the indicators the report needs.
Plan the work in a four-phase roadmap from cleaning to presentation.
result: A cleaner country-level dataset and a report organised around indicators and trends.
scope: Uses public indicator data. The repository link will be added once published.

title: SQL Data Warehouse (Course Project)
credit: Course project by Data With Baraa. Built as practice; the original design belongs to the course author.
summary: A guided SQL data warehouse build following the Data With Baraa course, used to practise layered warehouse design end to end.
question: Following an experienced engineer's full build is a fast way to learn the order of decisions in a warehouse project.
approach: Follow the course build from source systems to the final layer.
Rewrite each step in my own words in the documentation.
Compare the approach with my own coffee shop warehouse.
result: In progress. Shared with clear credit to the course author.
scope: Learning project. Not presented as original design.
